headline: Argentina Beat Switzerland 3-1 After Extra Time
whyCareReason: Champions against Swiss organisation: a quarter-final defined by patience, quality, and extra-time ruthlessness.
teaser: Argentina needed extra time to break Swiss resistance and seal a 3-1 quarter-final win in Kansas City.
story:
Switzerland did what Switzerland do: compact shape, disciplined distances, and almost zero clear chances conceded before the hour mark. Argentina monopolised the ball and waited for the moment the Swiss block stretched.

That moment arrived late and then again in extra time. Well-timed combinations opened the scoring and a third goal closed the contest. Switzerland pushed numbers forward, but Argentina's game management was ruthless once the lead was secured.

The 3-1 result after extra time sends the holders into the semi-finals. Switzerland exit after a campaign built on structure and giant-killing ambition.
stakes: A place in the World Cup semi-finals. Argentina stay on course; Switzerland's run ends in the last eight.
rivalryAngle: Organisation versus invention: Switzerland try to suffocate, Argentina try to unlock.
funFacts: Argentina are affectionately known as the La Albiceleste.
Switzerland are affectionately known as the Nati.
This high-profile match was held at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City on 2026-07-11.

keyPlayers.name: Lautaro Martínez
keyPlayers.hook: The key playmaker leading the tactical setup for the La Albiceleste.

keyPlayers.name: Granit Xhaka
keyPlayers.hook: The creative spark expected to make the difference for the Nati.

headToHead: Historically, matches between these two nations have always been tightly contested affairs, with tactical discipline proving key.
